title: How the Plan Class under Prescription Insurance on File Governs Copay Cards, Rewards, Discount Programs and Review Overrides
content:
The plan class on file under **Prescription Insurance on File** changes what other Kestrel programs may do for the same fill.

## Standing rules

- **Manufacturer copay cards.** Where the class is a government program, no manufacturer copay card is applied to a claim billed to that plan; and where the class does not allow a manufacturer copay card as secondary, Savings & Copay Assistance Programs treats the fill as ineligible for card benefits.
- **Rewards points.** Where the class does not allow rewards points on prescriptions, fills billed to that plan earn no points under Kestrel Care Rewards.
- **Discount program in lieu of the plan.** Where the class allows it, the patient may choose, before the claim is billed, to pay through a Kestrel discount program instead; that fill is then not billed to the plan at all, and its cost does not count toward the plan's deductible or out-of-pocket totals. Where the class does not allow it, the covered fill is always billed to the plan.
- **Drug utilization review rejection.** Where the class allows a pharmacist override, a drug utilization review rejection may be resubmitted on the drug utilization review override basis after the pharmacist reviews it; otherwise the prescriber must clarify.

## Condition and result

| Class setting | When it is Yes | When it is No |
|---|---|---|
| Discount program in lieu of the plan | Patient may choose the discount program before billing; fill not billed to the plan; cost outside deductible and out-of-pocket totals | Covered fill always billed to the plan |
| Pharmacist override of a drug utilization review rejection | Resubmitted on the override basis after pharmacist review | Prescriber must clarify |
| Rewards points on prescriptions | — | No Kestrel Care Rewards points on fills billed to that plan |
| Government program | No manufacturer copay card applied to a claim billed to that plan | — |

A dash marks a combination on which this rule states nothing.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A patient with a Medicare Part D Standard Plan asks, before a fill is billed, to use a Kestrel discount program. The class allows it, so the fill is not billed to the plan, and what the patient pays through the discount program does not count toward the plan's deductible or out-of-pocket totals.
